GUIDANCE ANALYSIS: Hays plc — H1 2025

METRIC: Germany Temp & Contracting year-on-year net-fee headwind
GUIDANCE TYPE: Qualitative
NUMERICAL GUIDANCE: None stated; use management rationale only
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Q3 FY25
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Quarter
BASIS: Year-on-year Temp & Contracting net-fee outlook in Germany.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- The year-on-year headwind is expected to be modest because of an easier comparator.
- Germany Temp & Contracting average hours worked remained sequentially stable.
- Automotive-related weakness continues to affect Temp, while Contracting is more resilient.

METRIC: Group net-fee growth working-day effect
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: c.1% positive impact on year-on-year net-fee growth
UNIT: %
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Q3 FY25
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Quarter
BASIS: Group year-on-year net-fee growth; calendar/working-day effect.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Easter falls entirely in Q4 FY25, whereas it was evenly split between Q3 and Q4 in FY24.

METRIC: Group net-fee growth working-day effect
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: c.1% headwind to year-on-year net-fee growth
UNIT: %
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Q4 FY25
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Quarter
BASIS: Group year-on-year net-fee growth; calendar/working-day effect.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Easter falls entirely in Q4 FY25, whereas it was evenly split between Q3 and Q4 in FY24.

METRIC: Group consultant headcount
GUIDANCE TYPE: Qualitative
NUMERICAL GUIDANCE: None stated; use management rationale only
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Q3 FY25
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Quarter
BASIS: Group consultant closing headcount.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Management expects headcount to remain broadly stable.
- Capacity reductions are planned in more difficult markets, offset by selective investment where opportunities exist.

METRIC: Group total headcount
GUIDANCE TYPE: Qualitative
NUMERICAL GUIDANCE: None stated; use management rationale only
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Q3 FY25
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Quarter
BASIS: Total Group headcount.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Management expects total headcount to decrease slightly as back-office efficiency programmes continue.

METRIC: Cost base per period
GUIDANCE TYPE: Qualitative
NUMERICAL GUIDANCE: None stated; use management rationale only
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: H2 FY25
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Half Year
BASIS: Periodic Group cost base; expected reductions are primarily from structural efficiencies in non-consultant areas.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Further structural cost efficiencies are expected to reduce the cost base per period.
- Back-office efficiency and operational restructuring programmes remain in progress.

METRIC: Exceptional costs
GUIDANCE TYPE: Qualitative
NUMERICAL GUIDANCE: None stated; use management rationale only
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: H2 FY25
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Half Year
BASIS: Exceptional restructuring and transformation costs.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Management expects further exceptional costs from ongoing multi-year restructuring, technology-transformation and finance-transformation programmes.

METRIC: Net finance charge
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: c.£13 million
UNIT: GBP million
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: FY25
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Expected Group net finance charge.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Higher average drawings on the revolving credit facility are expected to increase bank interest payable.

METRIC: Effective tax rate
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: c.32%
UNIT: %
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: FY25
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Pre-exceptional Group effective tax rate.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Guidance assumes no material change in the geographic mix of profits.

METRIC: Capital expenditure
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: c.£25 million
UNIT: GBP million
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: FY25
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Expected full-year Group capital expenditure.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Capital expenditure includes continued investment in technology infrastructure and cyber security.

METRIC: Enterprise net fees
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: approximately £225-250 million
UNIT: GBP million
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: FY25
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Enterprise net fees.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Management expects Enterprise fees to remain stable versus the FY23 peak, contrasting with broader labour-market conditions.
- Drivers include in-contract growth, higher fill rates, geographic expansion, new client wins and contract retention.

METRIC: Structural back-office cost savings
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: c.£30 million per annum
UNIT: GBP million per annum
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: By the end of FY27
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Multi Year
BASIS: Annualised structural back-office efficiency savings.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- The programme covers finance and technology functions, including finance transformation, technology outsourcing and global marketing restructuring.

METRIC: Germany efficiency-programme annual savings
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: more than £20 million in annual savings
UNIT: GBP million per annum
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: FY25
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Germany efficiency programme; annual savings target.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Actions include management delayering and reorganisation of sales and back-office operations.

METRIC: Pension scheme expenses and true-up costs
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: c.£6 million
UNIT: GBP million
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Next 12-18 months through to final scheme buy-out
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Date Range
BASIS: Expected post-buy-in pension-scheme expenses and true-up costs.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Costs relate to administration and true-up items as the Group progresses to final scheme buy-out and wind-up.

METRIC: Free-cash-flow benefit from pension buy-in
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: c.£19 million per annum
UNIT: GBP million per annum
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: From FY26
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Multi Year
BASIS: Annual cash-flow benefit from cessation of pension deficit contributions following the full pension buy-in.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- There will be no further pension-deficit contributions after the full buy-in.

METRIC: Net finance charge benefit from pension buy-in
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: approximately £1.5 million annual reduction
UNIT: GBP million per annum
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: From FY26
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Multi Year
BASIS: Annual reduction in the interest line from the pension-deficit-related charge.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- The pension-deficit interest charge is expected to fall away following the full buy-in.

METRIC: Business-line conversion rate
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: at least 25%
UNIT: %
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Normal market conditions
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Other
BASIS: Pre-central-cost conversion rate; net fees converted into pre-exceptional operating profit.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Management expects all business lines to be capable of this level in normal market conditions.

METRIC: Group conversion rate
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: 22-25%
UNIT: %
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Normal market conditions
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Other
BASIS: Overall Group conversion rate; net fees converted into pre-exceptional operating profit.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- This is management's normal-market operating target, supported by improved business-line prioritisation, resource allocation and scalable support functions.

METRIC: UK&I reallocated consultant fee productivity
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: more than £10k fee productivity per period
UNIT: GBP thousand per period
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Within 12 months
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Multi Year
BASIS: Expected productivity for more than 50 Healthcare and Social Care consultants reallocated to Construction & Property and Senior Finance.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Consultants were moved from lower-productivity, lower-conversion roles to specialisms with higher productivity potential.

METRIC: UK&I reallocated consultant conversion rate
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: mid-teens percentage conversion rate
UNIT: %
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Within 12 months
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Multi Year
BASIS: Expected conversion rate for more than 50 Healthcare and Social Care consultants reallocated to Construction & Property and Senior Finance.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- The consultants were transferred from roles with a 5% conversion rate to higher-potential specialisms.

METRIC: Operating profit growth, net-fee growth and headcount growth relationship
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: Operating profit growth should be greater than net-fee growth, which should exceed headcount growth
UNIT: relative growth relationship
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Through the cycle
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Multi Year
BASIS: Management's Golden Rule for operating performance and investment.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Management intends to retain structural cost savings, maintain disciplined consultant-headcount investment and generate healthy profit drop-through during an upturn.

METRIC: Group operating profit
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: return to, and then exceed, previous peak profits of £250 million
UNIT: GBP million
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Long-term objective
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Multi Year
BASIS: Long-term Group operating-profit objective; operating profit before exceptional items.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Management cites business-line prioritisation, optimised resource allocation and scaling the eight Focus countries as the route to achieving this objective.

METRIC: Net cash position
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: £100 million
UNIT: GBP million
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Not explicitly stated
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Not Stated
BASIS: Target net-cash position within the Group's capital-allocation framework.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Management's cash priorities are to fund investment and development, maintain a strong balance sheet, support a sustainable progressive core dividend and return surplus cash subject to the economic outlook.

METRIC: Perm job flow and activity
GUIDANCE TYPE: Qualitative
NUMERICAL GUIDANCE: None stated; use management rationale only
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Not explicitly stated
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Not Stated
BASIS: Group market and operating outlook, particularly for EMEA, UK&I and Germany.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Perm job flow and activity are expected to remain tough, particularly in France, UK&I and Germany.
- Slower client and candidate decision-making is extending time-to-hire.

COMPARABLE EARNINGS ANALYSIS: Hays plc — H1 2026
STRICT REPORT WINDOW: 2026-01-13 to 2026-02-26

COMPARABLE: PageGroup plc (PAGE)
REPORT DATE: 2026-01-13
REPORTED PERIOD: Q4 and FY 2025 trading update (quarter ended 31 December 2025)
WHY COMPARABLE: Direct international specialist recruiter with permanent, temporary and interim placement activities. Its professional-recruitment model and meaningful exposure to the UK, Germany, France and Australia make client hiring confidence, placement conversion, permanent-versus-temporary mix and recruiter productivity directly relevant transmission channels.
SHARED EXPOSURES:
- Professional-hiring demand and client/candidate confidence
- UK and continental-European hiring conditions
- Permanent versus temporary/interim recruitment mix
- Placement-conversion timing and fee-rate/pricing environment
TRANSFERABLE EARNINGS POINTS:
- Subdued client and candidate confidence, including delayed client hiring decisions [MACRO, NEGATIVE]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: Q4 group gross profit, PageGroup's fee-income measure, declined 4.6% year on year at constant currency. EMEA gross profit fell 8.9%; the UK fell 10.1%. Management said tighter recruitment budgets made clients more risk-averse, slowing time-to-hire, while offer-to-placement conversion remained the principal challenge.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: Negative for Hays net fees where professional clients defer requisitions or candidates do not convert accepted offers into completed placements. The magnitude should not be copied: Hays has a different country mix and greater relative Temp & Contracting exposure.
  SOURCE: https://www.page.com/sites/page-group-v3/files/2026-01/q4-2025-trading-update-transcript.pdf
- Permanent recruitment was weaker than temporary/interim recruitment in weak European markets [INDUSTRY, NEGATIVE]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: In PageGroup's French business, Q4 temporary recruitment gross profit declined 11%, versus a 22% decline in permanent recruitment. Across EMEA, interim recruitment was the most resilient business and grew 1%, while the region declined 8.9% overall.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: Negative primarily for Hays permanent-placement net fees and operating-profit conversion, partly offset where temporary and contracting demand remains relatively resilient. This is a mix signal rather than a forecast of a matching Group decline.
  SOURCE: https://www.page.com/sites/page-group-v3/files/2026-01/q4-2025-trading-update-transcript.pdf
EARNINGS SOURCE: https://www.page.com/sites/page-group-v3/files/2026-01/q4-2025-trading-update-transcript.pdf
EARNINGS SOURCE: https://www.londonstockexchange.com/news-article/PAGE/fourth-quarter-2025-trading-update/17410109

COMPARABLE: ManpowerGroup Inc. (MAN)
REPORT DATE: 2026-01-29
REPORTED PERIOD: Q4 2025 (three months ended 31 December 2025)
WHY COMPARABLE: Global workforce-solutions provider with temporary staffing, permanent recruitment, professional talent (Experis) and RPO operations. It shares European client-demand, permanent-recruitment and staffing-margin exposures, although its larger industrial/generalist staffing mix limits direct comparability to Hays.
SHARED EXPOSURES:
- European hiring demand
- Permanent recruitment activity
- Staffing bill-pay spread and gross-margin conditions
- France, Northern Europe and Asia-Pacific workforce-services demand
TRANSFERABLE EARNINGS POINTS:
- Softer-than-expected permanent recruitment activity in Europe [INDUSTRY, NEGATIVE]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: Q4 gross profit margin was 16.3%. Management attributed this in part to softer-than-expected European permanent-recruitment activity, while year-on-year staffing-margin trends were stable versus the preceding quarter.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: Negative read-through for Hays permanent-placement fees and mix, with less direct implication for Hays temporary/contracting net fees. Stable staffing margins indicate that the signal is more demand/mix-led than a broad bill-pay spread deterioration.
  SOURCE: https://investor.manpowergroup.com/node/68686/pdf
- European demand stabilized unevenly, with France sequentially improving but Northern Europe still soft [MACRO, MIXED]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: Group organic constant-currency revenue increased 2% in Q4. Management described stabilization in North America and Europe and sequential improvement in France; reported constant-currency revenue was down 3.4% in France and down 1.1% in Northern Europe, while Italy grew 6.4%.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: Mixed. The evidence argues against applying a uniform European deterioration to Hays: conditions varied materially by country. It modestly supports a cautious stance on northern-European professional demand while recognizing improving pockets in southern Europe.
  SOURCE: https://investor.manpowergroup.com/node/68686/pdf
EARNINGS SOURCE: https://investor.manpowergroup.com/node/68686/pdf
EARNINGS SOURCE: https://investor.manpowergroup.com/events/event-details/manpowergroup-fourth-quarter-2025-earnings-call

COMPARABLE: Robert Half Inc. (RHI)
REPORT DATE: 2026-01-29
REPORTED PERIOD: Q4 2025 (three months ended 31 December 2025)
WHY COMPARABLE: Specialist provider of contract talent and permanent placement in finance, accounting, technology, legal, marketing and administrative functions. Its professional-skills focus and permanent/contract model are directly relevant, though its United States weighting and consulting segment make geographic and portfolio exposure materially different from Hays.
SHARED EXPOSURES:
- Professional-services client hiring demand
- Permanent-placement volumes
- Contract-talent demand and pricing
- Hiring-decision timing and macroeconomic confidence
TRANSFERABLE EARNINGS POINTS:
- Subdued professional hiring and quits, despite improving macro confidence and client engagement [MACRO, MIXED]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: Fourth-quarter adjusted enterprise revenue was down 7% year on year, but management reported the first same-day constant-currency sequential growth since early 2022. It said hiring and quit rates remained subdued, while decision timelines were beginning to shorten as clients revisited postponed initiatives.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: Mixed for Hays: the year-on-year contraction supports caution on professional net fees, but the improving sequential engagement signal reduces confidence in extrapolating a worsening trend into Hays. The US-specific macro backdrop should receive a low weight.
  SOURCE: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315213/000031521326000003/rhiq42025ex991.htm
  SOURCE: https://www.roberthalf.com/content/dam/roberthalf/documents/us/en/indexed/investor-center/quarterly-conference-calls/RH_Q4%202025%20Prepared%20Remarks.pdf
- Contract-talent demand remained weak year on year, while bill rates held up [INDUSTRY, MIXED]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: Contract-talent revenue declined 9.0% in Q4 on an adjusted basis, but contract-talent bill rates increased 3.2% year on year after adjustment for specialization, currency and country mix. Contract gross margin was 39.2%, versus 39.1% a year earlier.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: The volume signal is negative for Hays Temp & Contracting demand, but resilient bill rates and gross margin indicate no direct evidence of broad pricing erosion. It therefore does not justify a mechanical margin reduction for Hays.
  SOURCE: https://www.roberthalf.com/content/dam/roberthalf/documents/us/en/indexed/investor-center/quarterly-conference-calls/RH_Q4%202025%20Prepared%20Remarks.pdf
EARNINGS SOURCE: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315213/000031521326000003/rhiq42025ex991.htm
EARNINGS SOURCE: https://www.roberthalf.com/content/dam/roberthalf/documents/us/en/indexed/investor-center/quarterly-conference-calls/RH_Q4%202025%20Prepared%20Remarks.pdf

COMPARABLE: Randstad N.V. (RAND)
REPORT DATE: 2026-02-11
REPORTED PERIOD: Q4 and FY 2025 (Q4 ended 31 December 2025)
WHY COMPARABLE: One of the closest global listed workforce-services comparables: it operates professional, digital, operational, enterprise/RPO, permanent and temporary staffing models across Europe, the UK and Australia. The professional-demand, permanent-hiring, European-country and temp-margin channels are directly relevant, although Randstad has a substantially larger operational staffing mix.
SHARED EXPOSURES:
- Professional and digital hiring demand
- Permanent-hiring confidence
- Germany, France, Northern Europe and UK-related European demand
- Temporary-staffing margin and wage/bill-rate dynamics
TRANSFERABLE EARNINGS POINTS:
- Low hiring confidence constrained permanent and professional recruitment [MACRO, NEGATIVE]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: Q4 organic revenue declined 2.1% Group-wide. In North America, professional revenue declined 10% and permanent hiring declined 14%, with management describing hiring confidence as low. Across the Group, professional revenue declined 8%; management said permanent contribution reduced gross margin by 20 basis points as key permanent markets remained challenging.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: Negative for Hays' professional and permanent-placement net fees and for gross-profit mix. This is directionally relevant but should not be applied percentage-for-percentage because Hays' country, discipline and contract mix differ.
  SOURCE: https://www.randstad.com/q4-report-2025/
  SOURCE: https://www.randstad.com/s3fs-media/rscom/public/2026-02/Q4_2025_Earnings_Call_Transcript.pdf?VersionId=9RG1P_yte9pVnAPDiaXyDmQS70p8C7Wz
- Weak German automotive and professional demand, with manufacturing showing initial stabilization [INDUSTRY, MIXED]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: Germany revenue declined 10%, driven by subdued automotive demand, although management said manufacturing was stabilizing. In France, professional revenue declined 14%, with political uncertainty pressuring confidence; the SME segment was down double digits while industrial Inhouse grew 13%.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: Mixed but net negative for Hays' German and French professional recruitment exposure. It indicates sector and client-size dispersion: professional/SME demand was weak, whereas selected industrial/operational pockets were more resilient.
  SOURCE: https://www.randstad.com/s3fs-media/rscom/public/2026-02/Q4_2025_Earnings_Call_Transcript.pdf?VersionId=9RG1P_yte9pVnAPDiaXyDmQS70p8C7Wz
- Temporary-staffing margin pressure and geographic mix divergence [INDUSTRY, NEGATIVE]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: Randstad reported a 20-basis-point year-on-year decline in temporary margin. Management cited greater resilience in operational staffing than in professional/digital specializations and weaker Northern Europe relative to Southern Europe; overall gross profit declined 4% while revenue declined 2.1%.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: Cautious negative read-through to Hays' net-fee conversion and operating profit, especially if professional activity underperforms temporary/operational staffing. It is not evidence that Hays faces the same margin decline, because the cited mix and country effects are not identical.
  SOURCE: https://www.randstad.com/q4-report-2025/
  SOURCE: https://www.randstad.com/s3fs-media/rscom/public/2026-02/Q4_2025_Earnings_Call_Transcript.pdf?VersionId=9RG1P_yte9pVnAPDiaXyDmQS70p8C7Wz
EARNINGS SOURCE: https://www.randstad.com/press/2026/fy-2025-perform-transform/
EARNINGS SOURCE: https://www.randstad.com/s3fs-media/rscom/public/2026-02/Q4_2025_Earnings_Call_Transcript.pdf?VersionId=9RG1P_yte9pVnAPDiaXyDmQS70p8C7Wz
EARNINGS SOURCE: https://www.randstad.com/q4-report-2025/

COMPARABLE: The Adecco Group AG (ADEN)
REPORT DATE: 2026-02-25
REPORTED PERIOD: Q4 and FY 2025 (Q4 ended 31 December 2025)
WHY COMPARABLE: Global workforce-solutions provider with flexible placement, permanent placement, outsourcing, MSP and professional/technology operations. It shares UK, Germany, France, Australia/New Zealand, client-demand, permanent-placement and staffing-pricing exposures; its growth was also affected by company-specific market-share gains, which are excluded from the read-through.
SHARED EXPOSURES:
- Flexible versus permanent placement mix
- UK, France, Germany and Australia/New Zealand demand
- Staffing pricing and bill-to-pay spread
- Client-sector demand including logistics, public sector, IT and financial services
TRANSFERABLE EARNINGS POINTS:
- Permanent-placement demand remained weaker than flexible placement demand [INDUSTRY, NEGATIVE]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: Adecco's Q4 permanent-placement revenue declined 6%, while flexible-placement revenue increased 4%. The company reported that lower permanent-placement volumes contributed to its gross-margin outcome.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: Negative for Hays' permanent fees relative to Temp & Contracting. The positive flexible-placement result supports the view that contracting can cushion, but not eliminate, weaker professional permanent-hiring conditions.
  SOURCE: https://www.adeccogroup.com/-/media/project/Adecco-Group/adeccogroup/PDF-Files/2026-Feb/Adecco-Group-Q425-Results-Prepared-Remarks_Transcript.pdf
- Firm staffing pricing, but uneven UK and French end-market demand [INDUSTRY, MIXED]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: Management said flex pricing remained firm with a positive bill-to-pay spread. In the UK and Ireland, revenue declined 1%, pressured by lower logistics and public-sector demand despite strength in IT technology and financial services. French revenue declined 2%, as logistics weighed while autos and manufacturing were strong.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: Mixed. Firm pricing is supportive of Hays' temporary/contracting fee conversion, while the UK and French sector split warns that client demand remained uneven. Adecco's market-share gains and cost savings are excluded and are not attributed to Hays.
  SOURCE: https://www.adeccogroup.com/-/media/project/Adecco-Group/adeccogroup/PDF-Files/2026-Feb/Adecco-Group-Q425-Results-Prepared-Remarks_Transcript.pdf
EARNINGS SOURCE: https://www.adeccogroup.com/-/media/project/Adecco-Group/adeccogroup/PDF-Files/2026-Feb/Adecco-Group-Q425-Results-Prepared-Remarks_Transcript.pdf
EARNINGS SOURCE: https://www.adeccogroup.com/investors/results-and-reports

PRELIMINARY COMPARABLE-ONLY METRIC ADD-ONS:
- Net fees: 0 GBPm (NEUTRAL)
  CALCULATION: 0.0 GBPm. The qualifying releases provide non-homogeneous measures: PageGroup reports gross profit; Randstad, ManpowerGroup, Adecco and Robert Half principally report revenue, gross margin or EBITA. Their demand signals are directionally useful but no qualifying comparable supplies a validated Hays net-fee transmission ratio, Hays-equivalent geographic/discipline weighting, or a permitted Hays starting net-fee base. Under the instruction to return zero where no defensible mapping exists, the signed comparable-only add-on is therefore 0.0 GBPm rather than a mechanically scaled peer percentage.
  ASSUMPTION: Only releases dated 2026-01-13 through 2026-02-26 were considered.
  ASSUMPTION: Peer-reported revenue, gross-profit and margin changes are not interchangeable with Hays net fees.
  ASSUMPTION: No target-company result, consensus estimate, post-cutoff information, stock-price reaction, or peer-specific market-share/cost-action effect is used in the calculation.
  ASSUMPTION: A non-zero GBPm output would require an externally imposed Hays fee base and a modelled country, discipline, perm/temp and timing elasticity; neither is evidenced solely by the qualifying comparable releases.
  SOURCE: https://www.page.com/sites/page-group-v3/files/2026-01/q4-2025-trading-update-transcript.pdf
  SOURCE: https://investor.manpowergroup.com/node/68686/pdf
  SOURCE: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315213/000031521326000003/rhiq42025ex991.htm
  SOURCE: https://www.randstad.com/q4-report-2025/
  SOURCE: https://www.adeccogroup.com/-/media/project/Adecco-Group/adeccogroup/PDF-Files/2026-Feb/Adecco-Group-Q425-Results-Prepared-Remarks_Transcript.pdf
- Pre-exceptional basic EPS: 0 GBp (NEUTRAL)
  CALCULATION: 0.00 GBp. A comparable-only EPS bridge would require a defensible mapping from peer operating-demand and pricing indicators to Hays pre-exceptional operating profit, then to Hays interest, tax and weighted-average share count. Those target-specific mappings are not disclosed by the qualifying peer releases. Therefore: comparable-only EPS add-on = 0.00 GBp.
  ASSUMPTION: The releases show mixed demand signals, but peer EPS incorporates each issuer's own capital structure, tax rate, exceptional items and share count.
  ASSUMPTION: Peer-specific restructuring, acquisition, pension, tax and capital-structure items are excluded.
  ASSUMPTION: No target-company tax, finance-cost or share-count assumption is imported to manufacture a non-zero EPS effect.
  SOURCE: https://www.page.com/sites/page-group-v3/files/2026-01/q4-2025-trading-update-transcript.pdf
  SOURCE: https://investor.manpowergroup.com/node/68686/pdf
  SOURCE: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315213/000031521326000003/rhiq42025ex991.htm
  SOURCE: https://www.randstad.com/q4-report-2025/
  SOURCE: https://www.adeccogroup.com/-/media/project/Adecco-Group/adeccogroup/PDF-Files/2026-Feb/Adecco-Group-Q425-Results-Prepared-Remarks_Transcript.pdf
- Pre-exceptional operating profit: 0 GBPm (NEUTRAL)
  CALCULATION: 0.0 GBPm. A non-zero operating-profit add-on would require a permitted conversion from an inferred Hays net-fee change into incremental operating profit. The qualifying releases demonstrate that temporary margins, permanent mix, country mix, pricing and cost actions differed substantially by peer; no peer release provides a validated Hays incremental conversion rate. Thus: comparable-only operating-profit add-on = 0.0 GBPm.
  ASSUMPTION: The adverse common signals are weaker professional/permanent demand and slower placement conversion; the offsets are resilient temporary/flexible demand and largely firm pricing in selected markets.
  ASSUMPTION: Peer structural cost savings, restructuring, productivity programs, market-share gains, acquisitions and other execution-specific items are excluded rather than transferred to Hays.
  ASSUMPTION: The reports cover calendar Q4 2025, which overlaps only part of Hays H1 2026; no timing multiplier is imposed without a comparable-only evidential basis.
  SOURCE: https://www.page.com/sites/page-group-v3/files/2026-01/q4-2025-trading-update-transcript.pdf

events.title: FY25 trading deterioration culminates in reduced operating-profit expectation
events.summary: Hays first reported Q3 FY25 like-for-like group net-fee growth of -9%, comprising Temp & Contracting -6% and Permanent -14%. It cited weak permanent hiring, longer hiring cycles and subdued German temporary staffing demand linked to automotive exposure; its periodic cost base had reduced to about £76 million, while FY25 operating-profit guidance remained in line with consensus at that time. In its June pre-close update, Hays said activity had weakened sequentially and expected Q4 like-for-like net fees to decline 9%, including a 14% fall in permanent fees. It reduced its expected FY25 pre-exceptional operating profit to about £45 million, versus then company-compiled consensus of £56.4 million, citing high profit drop-through because costs were largely fixed in the short term. Germany was expected to decline 5%, with weakness also in UK&I and ANZ permanent recruitment.
source_headlines: Hays reports Q3 FY25 net-fee decline as permanent hiring and German automotive-linked temp demand remain weak
Hays cuts FY25 profit expectation to about £45m after a broad-based deterioration in permanent recruitment

events.title: UK recruitment-market contraction and rising temporary pay growth
events.summary: The KPMG/REC UK Report on Jobs reported that permanent placements and temporary billings continued to decline in April 2025, while worker demand and vacancies fell further. Respondents cited weak employer confidence and tighter hiring budgets. Temporary-pay growth accelerated to an 11-month high, with respondents referring to recent minimum-wage increases.
source_headlines: KPMG/REC survey reports continued UK recruitment contraction and falling vacancies in April

events.title: FY25 results report lower net fees and profit, exceptional transformation charges and cost-savings plan
events.summary: For FY25, Hays reported net fees of £972.4 million, down 13% on a reported basis and 11% like for like, and pre-exceptional operating profit of £45.6 million, down 57% reported. It recorded £30.7 million of exceptional charges: £17.7 million for restructuring and £13.0 million for technology and finance transformation. Hays completed office and business-line closures, refinanced its revolving credit facility, reduced the total dividend to 1.24p per share and targeted a further approximately £45 million of annual structural cost savings by FY29. It said the pension buy-in would be materially positive for free cash flow from FY26.
source_headlines: Hays FY25 results confirm steep profit decline, restructuring charges and a revised capital-allocation framework

events.title: Q1 FY26 net-fee decline with headcount and cost-base reductions
events.summary: Hays reported that Q1 FY26 group net fees fell 8% year on year on a like-for-like basis. Temp & Contracting fees declined 5% and permanent-recruitment fees declined 13%, as permanent markets continued to experience longer hiring cycles. Consultant net-fee productivity increased 7%, consultant headcount was 15% lower year on year, and the periodic cost base improved to about £74 million. Net debt was about £40 million at quarter-end, reflecting normal seasonal outflows and payment timing.
source_headlines: Hays Q1 FY26 net fees fall 8%; staffing reductions and cost actions partly offset weak permanent hiring

events.title: Germany raises statutory minimum wage from January 2026
events.summary: Germany's cabinet approved an increase in the statutory minimum wage to €13.90 per hour from €12.82 per hour, effective 1 January 2026. The ministry described the first-stage increase as 8.42%.
source_headlines: German government approves increase in statutory minimum wage to €13.90 per hour from January 2026

events.title: Q2 FY26 fee decline exceeds consensus expectation as German hiring weakens
events.summary: Reuters reported that Hays' Q2 FY26 like-for-like net fees fell 10%, compared with analysts' expectation of a 9% decline. Hays expected pre-exceptional operating profit for the six months ended December 2025 of about £20 million, approximately 21.6% below the prior year. Reuters attributed the quarterly weakness principally to technology and engineering hiring in Germany, alongside persistently weak global hiring and delayed recruitment decisions.
source_headlines: Hays posts a larger-than-expected Q2 FY26 fee decline as German technology and engineering hiring weakens

events.title: German labor demand and vacancies fall during 2025
events.summary: Germany's Federal Employment Agency said labor demand continued to decline during 2025 amid weak economic development. Average registered vacancies were 632,000, down 62,000 from 2024, and total reported jobs were 1.461 million, the lowest level in 25 years. The agency also reported higher unemployment and elevated use of short-time work.
source_headlines: German Federal Employment Agency says 2025 job vacancies fell to their lowest level in 25 years

metric_impacts.metric_total_calculation: Derived H1 2026 EPS forecast = 0.55p. Operating income £20.0m - H1 finance charge £6.0m = pre-tax income £14.0m; £14.0m x (1 - 38.0%) = £8.68m pre-exceptional net income; £8.68m / 1,590.2m shares x 100 = 0.546p, rounded to 0.55p. Signed change versus H1 2025 actual 0.81p = 0.55p - 0.81p = -0.26p. No subsequent event has a defensible incremental after-tax or per-share transmission beyond management guidance.

event_contributions.affected_line: Operating profit, net finance charge, tax and weighted-average shares.
event_contributions.transmission_path: Net fees and cost actions -> guided pre-exceptional operating profit -> less finance charge -> pre-tax income -> tax -> pre-exceptional net income -> basic EPS.
assumptions: The £20.0m H1 pre-exceptional operating-profit indication is the EPS operating-income anchor but EPS is derived rather than copied.
ANNUAL/RUN-RATE ROUTE for finance and tax: FY26 net finance charge guidance is c.£12m and FY26 ETR guidance is c.38%.
With no disclosed half-year finance phasing, finance charge is allocated evenly at £12.0m x 1/2 = £6.0m. This is a low-confidence phasing assumption; it is not an operating-profit assumption.
Tax is applied at management's FY26 c.38% ETR because no H1-specific tax guidance was available before the cutoff.
1,590.2m FY25 basic weighted-average shares are held flat: the limited employee-plan treasury purchases do not provide a defensible H1 weighted-average-share change.
Pre-exceptional treatment excludes the c.£10m H1 restructuring charge because the requested EPS metric is pre-exceptional.
event_contributions.calculation: Operating income = £20.0m. Pre-tax income = £20.0m - £6.0m + £0.0m = £14.0m. Net income = £14.0m x (1 - 38.0/100) + £0.0m = £8.68m. EPS = (£8.68m / 1,590.2m) x 100 = 0.546p, rounded to 0.55p. EPS change = 0.55p - 0.81p = -0.26p.

earnings_bridge.calculation: Linked H1 2026 net fees = £451.0m. Operating income = £451.0m x 4.4346% + £0.0m = £20.0m. Pre-tax income = £20.0m - £6.0m + £0.0m = £14.0m. Pre-exceptional net income = £14.0m x (1 - 38.0%) + £0.0m = £8.68m. Pre-exceptional basic EPS = (£8.68m / 1,590.2m) x 100 = 0.546p, rounded to 0.55p.
assumptions: The 4.4346% operating margin is implied by H1 management guidance: £20.0m / £451.0m.
FY26 finance-charge guidance of c.£12m is phased 50% into H1 because no more specific period allocation was disclosed; this is explicitly low confidence.
FY26 ETR guidance of c.38% is used without importing any post-cutoff reported H1 tax result.
The bridge is pre-exceptional: restructuring and transformation charges are excluded.

The 1,590.2m denominator is the latest disclosed basic weighted-average share count available before the cutoff; the schema field is labelled diluted_shares, but the requested output is basic EPS and therefore uses the basic denominator.
